| `payment-imputed-to` | To which obligation is the payment imputed (art. 6.1.12, 6.1.13)? | truth | `payment_imputed_to(pay: Payment, o: Obligation)` | `evaluate truth(payment_imputed_to(pay: <pay>, o: <o>));` | Article 6.1.12(1). The payment discharges first any expenses (`ExpensesDischargedFirst`); Article 6.1.12(3)(d). Failing that, payment is imputed to the obligation which has arisen first (`ImputationByEarliestOrigin`); Article 6.1.12(3)(a). In the absence of imputation, payment is imputed to an obligation which is due or which is the first to fall due (`ImputationByFirstDue`); Article 6.1.12(3)(b). Failing that, payment is imputed to the obligation for which the obligee has least security (`ImputationByLeastSecurity`); Article 6.1.12(3)(c). Failing that, payment is imputed to the obligation which is the most burdensome for the obligor (`ImputationByMostBurdensome`); Article 6.1.12(2). If the obligor makes no specification, the obligee may within a reasonable time declare the obligation to which it imputes the payment, provided that obligation is due and undisputed (`ImputationByObligeeDeclaration`); Article 6.1.12(1). An obligor owing several monetary obligations may specify at the time of payment the debt to which the payment is to be applied (`ImputationBySpecification`); Article 6.1.13. Article 6.1.12 applies with appropriate adaptations to the imputation of performance of non-monetary obligations (`ImputationOfNonMonetaryPerformance`); Article 6.1.12(1). The payment discharges then interest due and finally the principal (`InterestDischargedSecond`) | tests 1 |

- **Does not answer:** Which mandatory rules of the applicable law restrict the performance of the contract? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART6_1_14_EN). THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them, or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law; they do not replace the mandatory rules of the applicable law (article 1.4, hub `unidroit.picc`).
- **Does not answer:** What is the applicable rate of exchange and what does the public permission of a particular state require? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART6_1_9_EN, PICC_ART6_1_14_EN). THE RATE OF EXCHANGE AND THE CONTENT OF A PUBLIC PERMISSION ARE INPUTS OF THE CASE: articles 6.1.9 and 6.1.14–6.1.17 name the RULE OF CHOICE (which rate applies, who is to take the measures necessary to obtain the permission), while the number itself and the requirements of a particular state are brought by the case.
- **Does not answer:** How is a payment imputed where no criterion of the sequence applies? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART6_1_12_EN). THE ORDER OF IMPUTATION IS WRITTEN AS §116 PRIORITIES, NOT AS READING ORDER: expenses and interest come before the obligor's indication (article 6.1.12(1)), and the four criteria of paragraph 3 displace one another in the order the source declares. Proportional imputation where no criterion applies is not in the model: that is arithmetic over an indeterminate set of debts, and no case presents it.
- **Does not answer:** What is a reasonable time for performance after the conclusion of the contract? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART6_1_1_EN). THE PRINCIPLES HAVE NO CALENDAR: the "reasonable time" of article 6.1.1(c) is not converted into days by the model — it remains an evaluative element or a fact of the case.

- **Does not answer:** What does the Convention answer on renegotiation where performance becomes far more onerous? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART6_2_2_EN). HARDSHIP IS WHAT THE CONVENTION DOES NOT HAVE AS A RULE. Article 79 of the Convention knows an exemption from liability for an impediment beyond control, but provides for neither renegotiation nor adaptation of the contract by a court. Articles 6.2.1–6.2.3 give both; on the same facts the two instruments answer differently, and this is observed by case 04.
- **Does not answer:** Has the equilibrium of the contract been fundamentally altered and is it reasonable to adapt it? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART6_2_2_EN, PICC_ART6_2_3_EN). THE EVALUATIVE ELEMENTS OF CHAPTER 6 GO THROUGH THE §47.3 JUDGMENT CHANNEL with the organ `Tribunal`: the absence of a legitimate interest of the obligee in refusing performance (6.1.3, 6.1.5), the reasonableness of upholding the remaining contract where a permission affects some terms only (6.1.16, 6.1.17), a fundamental alteration of the equilibrium of the contract and the impossibility of taking the events into account at the time of conclusion (6.2.2), the reasonableness of termination or adaptation (6.2.3(4)). The model neither decides them nor substitutes a guess.
